diagnosis.summary: The nightly run 37f39097 for 2026-10-01 failed at ingest because orders.csv has a new column, coupon_code, that isn't in the raw.orders contract. All contract columns are present, values parse cleanly and the row count (440) is normal. The proposed fix is to ignore the extra coupon_code column on ingest and rerun.

root_cause.explanation: Upstream added a non-contract column coupon_code to the orders landing file starting 2026-10-01. Ingest compares the file's header to the contract and failed with 'unexpected columns [coupon_code]'. No contract columns are missing and the data looks healthy.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on raw.orders with a schema mismatch: no missing columns, one unexpected column (coupon_code)
The landing file has all contract columns plus coupon_code, 440 rows and no parse problems
440 rows is within the normal daily range (412-534) and coupon_code is not in the contract
No ingest overrides are set yet
Per the runbook, an unexpected-only mismatch means a new column was added, and the fix is ignore_extra_columns

alternatives_considered: Column renamed: ruled out because no contract column is missing
Partial or corrupt delivery: ruled out because the row count is normal and nothing failed to parse
dbt model change: ruled out because the run failed at ingest, before transform
Escalate to upstream: not needed because an extra column that isn't in the contract doesn't change what the existing contract columns mean

proposal.rationale: Upstream added a new non-contract column coupon_code to orders.csv. All contract columns are present, values parse normally, and the row count (440) is in the normal range. The runbook says to handle a new non-contract column with ignore_extra_columns.

applied: ingest now ignores upstream columns ['coupon_code'] on raw.orders
